The '''2013–14 season''' was [[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]'s [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|115th in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga#Seasons in La Liga|83rd consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. This was the first and only season under head coach [[Gerardo Martino]].

This season was the first since [[2006-07 FC Barcelona season|2006–07]] without teammate [[Eric Abidal]], who departed to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] after his contract expired.

==Season overview==

===June===
On 3 June, Brazilian [[Neymar]] was officially presented as a Barcelona player to more than 50,000 fans at [[Camp Nou]]. He joined the squad after the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in Brazil. On 20 June, after spending the previous season on loan to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], it was officially announced that [[Andreu Fontàs]] will be joining [[Celta de Vigo]] for a sum of €1&nbsp;million. Barça will retain a buy-back clause in addition to the player's rights in any future transfer. While at Celta, Fontàs will be reunited with former [[FC Barcelona B|Barcelona B]] coach [[Luis Enrique (footballer)|Luis Enrique]], whom he managed between 2008 and 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/andreu-fontas-to-make-the-move-to-celta-vigo |title=Andreu Fontàs to make the move to Celta Vigo |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=20 June 2013 |access-date=20 June 2013}}</ref> On 28 June, it was announced that Santos will participate in the 2013 edition of the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]] on 2 August at the Camp Nou. Santos' participation was agreed upon Barça signing Neymar.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/santos-fc-to-face-fc-barcelona-in-the-joan-gamper-trophy-on-august-2 |title=Santos FC to face FC Barcelona in the Joan Gamper Trophy |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 June 2013 |access-date=29 June 2013}}</ref>

===July===
On 6 July, [[Bojan Krkić|Bojan]] was officially loaned to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] with an option for a second year loan spell.<ref>{{cite news |title='Ajax huurt Bojan van Barcelona' (in Dutch)|url=http://www.nu.nl/sport/3519539/ajax-huurt-bojan-van-barcelona.html |work=ANP|publisher=NU.nl|date=6 July 2013 |access-date=6 July 2013}}</ref> Bojan explained that conversations with [[Johan Cruyff]] had influenced his decision to move to Ajax, as well as the opportunity to play in the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Officieel: Ajax huurt Bojan (in Dutch)|url=http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/hoofdnieuws/71546/officieel-ajax-huurt-bojan.html|work=Jules P|publisher=Ajax Showtime|date=6 July 2013|access-date=6 July 2013|archive-date=9 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130709022612/http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/hoofdnieuws/71546/officieel-ajax-huurt-bojan.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Cruijff en CL haalden Bojan over (in Dutch)|url=http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/hoofdnieuws/71552/cruijff-en-cl-haalden-bojan-over.html|work=Sam van Raalte|publisher=Ajax Showtime|date=6 July 2013|access-date=6 July 2013|archive-date=8 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130708023006/http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/hoofdnieuws/71552/cruijff-en-cl-haalden-bojan-over.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/bojan-krkic-on-loan-to-ajax |title=Bojan Krkic out on loan to Ajax |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=6 July 2013 |access-date=7 July 2013}}</ref> On 8 July, Barcelona announced the transfer of Spanish international forward [[David Villa]] to [[Atlético Madrid]] for a reported fee of €5.1&nbsp;million and reserve the right to 50% of any future sale of the player. Villa, who joined Barça in the summer of 2010, played 119 times and scored 48 goals and leaves the club after three seasons and eight trophies won.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/club-reach-deal-in-principal-to-sell-david-villa-to-atletico-madrid |title=David Villa joins Atlético Madrid |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 July 2013 |access-date=8 July 2013}}</ref> On 15 July, Barcelona announced that midfielder [[Thiago Alcântara|Thiago]] will be joining German champions [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], where he joins his former Barcelona coach [[Pep Guardiola]], for €25&nbsp;million. The transfer also stipulates that the two clubs will play a friendly sometime within the next four seasons. The 22-year-old leaves after two season with the first team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/thiago-alcantara-sold-to-bayern-munich-for-25-million-euros |title=Thiago Alcántara sold to Bayern Munich for 25 million euros |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=15 July 2013 |access-date=15 July 2013}}</ref> On 16 July, it was announced that midfielder [[Sergio Busquets]] agreed to a contract extension with the club for a further five years until 2018, with an option of an additional year. Busquets' buyout clause remains set at €150&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sergio-busquets-renews-until-2018 |title=Sergio Busquets renews until 2018 |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=16 July 2013 |access-date=16 July 2013}}</ref> On 19 July, Barcelona President [[Sandro Rosell]] officially announced the resignation of current manager [[Tito Vilanova]]. Vilanova will not be able to perform his managerial duties as he undergoes further treatment for his illness. During the press conference, Rosell announced, "After evaluating the results from the routine check-ups, which Tito Vilanova underwent this week, he was presented with the option to continue treatment to control his illness which will make it impossible to continue his responsibilities as the first team manager of the senior side."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tito-vilanova-will-not-continue-at-fc-barcelona |title=Tito Vilanova will not continue at FC Barcelona |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 July 2013 |access-date=19 July 2013}}</ref> As a result, Barça rescheduled their pre-season match against [[Lechia Gdańsk]] in Poland to 30 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/game-against-lechia-gdansk-rescheduled-for-july-30th |title=FC Barcelona will play in Gdansk on 30 July |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 July 2013 |access-date=19 July 2013}}</ref> On 23 July, former [[Newell's Old Boys]] manager [[Gerardo Martino]] was officially announced as the new coach of Barcelona and is subsequently signed a two-year contract with the club. The appointment makes Martino, nicknamed "Tata", the fourth Argentine to coach Barça after [[Helenio Herrera]], [[Roque Olsen]] and [[César Luis Menotti]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/gerardo-martino-new-coach-of-fc-barcelona |title=Gerardo Martino, new coach of FC Barcelona |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=23 July 2013 |access-date=23 July 2013}}</ref>

===August===
On 1 August, [[Cristian Tello]] extended his contract with Barcelona until 30 June 2018, with a set buyout clause of €25&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tello-extends-contract-till-2017-18 |title=Tello extends contract till 2017/18 |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 August 2013 |access-date=1 August 2013}}</ref>
On 18 August, Barcelona won their first match of the [[La Liga]] season thrashing [[Levante UD|Levante]] 7–0, with goals coming from [[Alexis Sánchez]], [[Dani Alves]] and [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] and [[Brace (sports)#In sports|braces]] by [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]].<ref>{{cite web|last=First match|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2013-2014/league/round-1/fc-barcelona_llevant-u-d|publisher=Fcbarcelona.com|title=FC Barcelona v Levante: Sensational!(7-0)|access-date=19 August 2013}}</ref> On 25 August, Barça defeated [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] with a single goal from [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] before the half-time break.<ref name="25 aug">{{cite web|title=FCB vs Malaga|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/116063/malaga-vs-fc-barcelona/report?ICID=OP|access-date=27 August 2013}}</ref> On 28 August, Barça won the [[2013 Supercopa de España]] at the Camp Nou. The 0–0 scoreline at Camp Nou, meant that the 1–1 draw from the first leg at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]] was enough to win the trophy on the away goals rule, with the winning goal coming from Neymar's 66th-minute header.<ref name="2013 Spanish Super cup">{{cite web|title=2013 Spanish Super cup|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2013-2014/supercopa-spanyol/final-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_at-madrid|publisher=fcbarcelona.com|access-date=29 August 2013}}</ref>

===September===
On 1 September, Barcelona made it three wins in a row to ensure top spot on the league table, after a hard-fought victory against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. Messi's first half hat-trick, together with a match saving performance by [[Víctor Valdés]], was enough to see Barça win at the [[Mestalla Stadium|Mestalla]] for the first time since 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/valencia-fc-barcelona-three-straight-wins-ahead-of-international-breakde-tres-en-tres-abans-de-laturada-2-3 |title=Barça win wild one at Mestalla |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 September 2013 |access-date=2 September 2013}}</ref> On 14 September, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 3–2 at Camp Nou with a 94th-minute winner from Alexis Sánchez.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/alexis-in-extremis-3-2 |title=Barça win it deep in stoppage time. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=14 September 2014 |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref> On 18 September, Barcelona defeated Ajax 4–0 at home in their first group match of the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League]] with a hat-trick from Messi and one goal from [[Gerard Piqué]]. With the three goals, Messi took his career tally to 62 goals in the Champions League leaving him [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Goalscoring|nine goals]] short of former [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] forward and record marksman [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]]. He also became the first player to score four hat-tricks in the Champions League, whilst also netting his 24th such treble for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-ajax-the-perfect-start-in-europe-4-0 |title=Perfect Champions League start. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 September 2013 |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref> On 21 September, Barcelona defeated [[Rayo Vallecano]] 0–4 at [[Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas|Campo de Vallecas]]. A hat-trick from Pedro, one from [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and another great performance from Valdés, who saved his second penalty in two consecutive matches, gave Barça the three points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/rayo-win-makes-it-five-wins-out-of-five-0-4 |title=Perfect start in La Liga continues. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 September 2013 |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref> This match also marked the first time since 7 May 2008 against Real Madrid where Barcelona did not finish the match with a higher percentage of possession than the opponent. Breaking a streak of 315 matches in a row. On 24 September, Barcelona continued its hot start to the league campaign with a 4–1 victory over [[Real Sociedad]] at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-r-sociedad-barcelona-in-festival-mood-4-1 |title=Barça make six wins out of six in the league. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=24 September 2013 |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref> On 28 September, Barcelona defeated newly promoted side [[UD Almería|Almería]] on the [[Estadio de los Juegos Mediterráneos|road]] with a 0–2 scoreline.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2013-2014/league/round-7/almeria_fc-barcelona |title=Record setting victory in Almería. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 September 2013 |access-date=29 September 2013}}</ref> With the victory, Barça set a team record with seven wins from the first seven matches in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/seven-straight-victories-in-la-liga-seal-new-club-record |title=Seven from seven to start the league campaign. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 September 2013 |access-date=29 September 2013}}</ref> Messi scored his [[2013–14 La Liga#Top goalscorers|league leading]] eight goal of the season but was substituted seven minutes later with muscle problems in his right leg. It was confirmed Messi will be out for two to three weeks with a tear to his [[biceps femoris]] in his right leg.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-out-for-two-to-three-weeks |title=Messi to miss 2-3 weeks due to right leg injury. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 September 2013 |access-date=29 September 2013}}</ref>

===October===
[[File:Barcelona FC arriving Glasgow (10036918023).jpg|thumb|right|Barça players arriving at [[Glasgow Airport]] before their clash with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]]]
On 1 October, Barcelona defeated Scottish club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Celtic Park]] with a 0–1 scoreline to stay at top of [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group H|Group H]] in the Champions League. Fàbregas' goal gave Barça the win, a year after last season's defeat in the same fixture.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2013-2014/champions-league/round-2-h/celtic_fc-barcelona |title=Barça stays top of Group H. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 October 2013 |access-date=1 October 2013}}</ref> On 5 October, Barcelona made it eight out of eight in their record breaking start to the league season with a 4–1 win over [[Real Valladolid]] at Camp Nou. Goals by Xavi, Neymar and a brace by Sánchez turned the result around after Valladolid's [[Javi Guerra (footballer, born 1982)|Javi Guerra]] opener in the tenth minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-valladolid-spectacular-comeback-4-1 |title=Barça keep winning. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=6 October 2013 |access-date=6 October 2013}}</ref> On 19 October, Barcelona drop their first points of the season after a goalless draw with [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] at [[El Sadar Stadium|El Sadar]] that draw mean Barça failed to match La Liga's best ever start to a season and put an end to an eight-game winning run.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-hit-the-buffers-in-pamplona-0-0 |title=Winning streak ends at Pamplona. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 October 2013 |access-date=19 October 2013}}</ref> On 22 October, Barcelona failed to clinch a spot in knockout rounds of the Champions League against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] after a 1–1 draw in Italy. Messi goal equaled the result after [[Robinho]] opener in the ninth minute. With the draw, Barça stayed top of Group H with seven points, two more than Milan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/ac-milan-fc-barcelona-point-keeps-barca-top-1-1 |title=Barça continue pace to qualified for knockout round of Champions League with draw in Milan. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=22 October 2013 |access-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> On 26 October, the first ''[[El Clásico|Clásico]]'' of the season was contested at the Camp Nou with Barça securing a 2–1 victory over their great rivals. Strikes from Neymar and a spectacular Sánchez second gave Barça the win that leaves them six points clear of Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-r-madrid-neymar-and-alexis-tip-the-clasico-barca-s-way-2-1 |title=Clásico victory for Barça. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=27 October 2013 |access-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> On 29 October, Barcelona defeated [[Celta de Vigo]] 3–0 at [[Balaídos]] with goals from Sánchez and Fàbregas to keep Barça undefeated in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/celta-vigo-v-fc-barcelona-and-three-more-0-3 |title=Victory in Vigo. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 October 2013 |access-date=22 October 2013}}</ref>

===November===
On 1 November, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 1–0 at Camp Nou and won the first [[Derbi barceloní|derby]] of the season the only goal came from Alexis Sánchez.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-espanyol-cronica-lliga-2013-14 |title=Derbi win for Barça. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 October 2013 |access-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> On 6 November, Barcelona defeated Milan 3–1 at Camp Nou and qualified for the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Knockout Rounds]] of the Champions League with two match days left. Messi returned to scoring with a brace after going four games without a goal. Busquets added another to send Barça through to the last 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-sees-fc-barcelona-through-to-last-16 |title=Barça's win clinch place in Knockout Round. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=7 November 2013 |access-date=22 November 2013}}</ref> On 10 November, Barcelona defeated [[Real Betis]] 1–4 at the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín|Benito Villamarín]] with scores from Neymar, Pedro and two from Fàbregas to put Barça three points ahead of Atlético Madrid in La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/betis-fc-barcelona-lead-at-the-top-increased-1-4 |title=Big win in Sevilla despite Messi's injury. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=11 November 2013}}</ref> Messi picked up an injury and will be sidelined for 6 to 8 weeks with a tear in his left [[hamstring]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-out-for-between-6-and-8-weeks |title=Messi done for 2013. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 November 2013 |access-date=11 November 2013}}</ref> On 23 November, Barcelona defeated [[Granada CF|Granada]] 4–0 at Camp Nou. Barça overcome their injury woes to beat Granada with two penalty goals from Iniesta, and Fàbregas, while Sánchez and Pedro scored the others.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-granada-cf-just-as-reliable-4-0 |title=FC Barcelona v Granada CF: Reliable as ever (4-0). |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 November 2013 |access-date=25 November 2013}}</ref> On 26 November, Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the season, a 2–1 loss to Ajax at the [[Amsterdam Arena]]. With the loss, Barça fell one victory short of equaling their best start to a season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/ajax-v-fc-barcelona-first-defeat-2-1|title=Ajax v FC Barcelona: First defeat (2-1). |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 November 2013 |access-date=28 November 2013}}</ref>

===December===
On 1 December, Barcelona lost to [[Athletic Bilbao]] at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés]] by a score of 1–0. This was Barcelona's second loss in a week and their first in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/athletic-bilbao-v-fc-barcelona-beaten-at-the-new-san-mames-1-0. |title=First lost in the league. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=7 December 2013 |access-date=7 December 2013}}</ref> On 6 December, Barcelona started their [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] campaign with a victory in [[Estadio Cartagonova|Cartagonova]] with a 1–4 win over [[FC Cartagena|Cartagena]]. Goals from Fàbregas, and [[Jean Marie Dongou|Dongou]], and a brace by Pedro, gave Barça the first leg victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-cartagena-v-fc-barcelona-lethal-reaction-1-4. |title=Winning start to the Copa del Rey. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=7 December 2013 |access-date=7 December 2013}}</ref> On 11 December, Barcelona defeated Celtic 6–1 at Camp Nou and secured the top spot in the group thanks to goals from Piqué, Pedro, Neymar (3) and Tello.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-celtic-fc-goals-galore-to-top-the-group-6-1. |title=Goals galore to top the group. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=13 December 2013 |access-date=13 December 2013}}</ref> On 14 December, Barcelona defeated [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 2–1 at Camp Nou two goals from Neymar gave Barça the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-villarreal-three-hard-earned-points-2-1. |title=Three hard earned points. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 December 2013 |access-date=17 December 2013}}</ref> On 17 December, Barcelona qualify for the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey#Round of 16|Round of 16]] of the Copa del Rey after defeating 3-0 Cartagena at the Camp Nou Pedro, Mariano [[Own goal|(o.g.)]] and Neymar scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-fc-cartagena-reaffirming-performance-3-0. |title=Reaffirming performance. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=20 December 2013 |access-date=20 December 2013}}</ref> On 22 December, Barcelona defeated [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] 2–5 at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]] a hat-trick from Pedro and a brace from Fàbregas gave Barça the victory over Getafe, who led 2–0 after 14 minutes. With the win, Barça stays top of the league into the holiday break and ends 2013, leading La Liga wire-to-wire.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/getafe-cf-fc-barcelona-pedro-and-cesc-lead-leaders-fightback-2-5. |title=Pedro and Cesc lead leaders' fightback. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=22 December 2013 |access-date=22 December 2013}}</ref>

===January===

On 5 January, Barcelona won their first match of the year against newly promoted side [[Elche CF|Elche]], with a 4–0 score. A hat-trick from Sánchez, including a goal from a free kick, and another from Pedro, gave Barça the win at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-elche-alexis-the-superstar-4-0 |title=Alexis the Superstar. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=5 January 2014 |access-date=5 January 2014}}</ref>
On 8 January, Barcelona defeated Getafe 4–0 in the first leg of the Round of 16 of the Copa del Rey. Braces from Fàbregas and Messi gave Barça half a ticket to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-getafe-killer-instinct-4-0 |title=Getafe: Killer instinct. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=10 January 2014}}</ref>
On 11 January, Barcelona were held to a scoreless draw by [[Atlético Madrid]] at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]] a gripping game between the two league leaders ended without score.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/atletico-madrid-v-fc-barcelona-thrills-but-no-goals-0-0 |title=Thrills but no goals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 January 2014 |access-date=18 January 2014}}</ref>
On 16 January, Barcelona qualify for the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey#Quarter-finals|Quarter-finals]] of the Copa del Rey after defeating 2-0 Getafe at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]] a brace from messi gave Barça the win and Xavi features in his 700th match for the team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/getafe-cf-fc-barcelona-through-to-the-quarter-finals-0-2 |title=Through to the quarter-finals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 January 2014 |access-date=18 January 2014}}</ref>
On 19 January, Barcelona drew their second league match in a row. A 1–1 draw against [[Levante UD|Levante]] at the [[Estadi Ciutat de València|Ciutat de València]] saw Gerard Piqué scoring the only goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/llevant-ud-fc-barcelona-out-of-luck-in-valencia-1-1 |title=Out of luck in Valencia. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=23 January 2014 |access-date=23 January 2014}}</ref> On 22 January, Barcelona defeated Levante 4–1 in the first leg of the Quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey three days after the draw in the league an own goal from Juanfran and a hat-trick from [[Cristian Tello]] gave Barça the win at the Ciutat de València.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/llevant-ud-fc-barcelona-tello-edges-fc-barcelona-closer-to-the-semi-finals-1-4 |title=Tello edges FC Barcelona closer to the semi-finals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=23 January 2014 |access-date=23 January 2014}}</ref>
On 26 January, Barcelona defeated [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] 3–0 at Camp Nou goals from Piqué, Pedro and Sánchez gave Barça the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-malaga-cf-brilliant-all-round-performance |title=brilliant all round performance. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 January 2014 |access-date=28 January 2014}}</ref>
On 29 January, Barcelona qualified for the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey#Semi-finals|Semi-finals]] of the Copa del Rey after defeating Levante 5–1 at the Camp Nou; Adriano, Puyol, Sánchez (2) and Fàbregas scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-levante-deluge-of-goals-and-to-the-semi-finals-5-1 |title=Deluge of goals and to the semi-finals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=31 January 2014 |access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Barcelona lost their first match at home after being defeated at Camp Nou by [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] with a scoreline of 2–3, where Sánchez and Messi scored for Barça, while [[Jordi Alba]] was sent off with a second yellow.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-valencia-winning-streak-over-2-3 |title=winning streak over. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=4 February 2014 |access-date=4 February 2014}}</ref> On 5 February, Barcelona defeated [[Real Sociedad]] 2–0 at Camp Nou in the first leg of the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey. goals from Busquets and Zubikarai [[Own goal|(o.g.)]] gave Barça half a ticket to the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-real-sociedad-vindication-2-0. |title=Vindication. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=6 February 2014 |access-date=6 February 2014}}</ref>
On 9 February, Barcelona defeated [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] 4–1 at [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]], goals coming from Sánchez, Fàbregas and a brace by Messi to
give Barça the top spot in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sevilla-fc-fc-barcelona-important-win-in-the-rain-1-4. |title=important win in the rain. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 February 2014 |access-date=10 February 2014}}</ref>
On 12 February, Barcelona reached their 35th Copa del Rey [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|final]] after a 1–1 draw against Real Sociedad at [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/real-sociedad-fc-barcelona-to-the-final-1-1. |title=To the final!. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 February 2014 |access-date=18 February 2014}}</ref> On 15 February, Barcelona trashed [[Rayo Vallecano]] 6–0 at Camp Nou with goals coming from Adriano, Sánchez, Pedro, Neymar and a brace by Lionel Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-rayo-vallecano-champagne-performance-6-0. |title=Champagne performance!. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 February 2014 |access-date=18 February 2014}}</ref> On 18 February, Barcelona defeated [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]] with a 0–2 win in their Champions League first leg encounter to move closer to qualifying for the quarter-finals. Messi and Dani Alves scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/manchester-city-fc-fc-barcelona-messi-and-alves-set-up-impressive-first-leg-win. |title=Messi and Alves set up impressive first leg win. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 February 2014 |access-date=19 February 2014}}</ref>
On 22 February, Barcelona lost to [[Real Sociedad]] at the [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]] by a score of 3–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/real-societat-fc-barcelona-step-backwards-at-anoeta-3-1. |title=Painful defeat at Anoeta. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 March 2014 |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref>

===March===
On 9 March, Barcelona defeated [[UD Almería|Almería]] 4–1 at Camp Nou; goals from Sánchez, Messi, Xavi and Puyol gave Barça the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-ud-almeria-reaction-with-goals-4-1. |title=Reaction with goals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 March 2014 |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref>
On 8 March, Barcelona lost to [[Real Valladolid]] at the [[Estadio Nuevo José Zorrilla|José Zorrilla]] by a score of 1–0. This was Barcelona's second away loss in a row.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/valladolid-v-fc-barcelona-disappointing-defeat-1-0. |title=Disappointing defeat. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 March 2014 |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref> On 12 March, Barcelona qualified for the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the Champions League after defeating Manchester City 2–1 at Camp Nou. Messi and Dani Alves scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-manchester-city-fc-back-on-track-2-1. |title=Back on track!. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 March 2014 |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref>
On 16 March, Barcelona trashed [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] 7–0 at Camp Nou with goals coming from Sánchez, Iniesta, Tello, Pedro and a hat-trick by Lionel Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-ca-osasuna-goalfest-7-0. |title=Goalfest!. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=17 March 2014 |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref>
On 23 March, the second [[El Clásico|Clásico]] of the season was contested at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] with Barça securing a 3–4 victory over their great rivals. A hat-trick from Messi and a lone goal by Iniesta gave Barça the win that leaves them one point off of league leaders [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/brilliant-barca-win-bernabeu-thriller-3-4. |title=Brilliant Barça win Bernabeu thriller. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 March 2014 |access-date=29 March 2014}}</ref>
On 26 March, Barcelona defeated [[Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] 3–0 at Camp Nou. A brace from Neymar and a lone goal by Messi gave Barça the win. Valdés picked up an injury and will be sidelined for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-celta-bitter-sweet-win-3-0. |title=Bittersweet win. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 March 2014 |access-date=29 March 2014}}</ref>
On 29 March, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 0–1 at [[Cornellà de Llobregat]] and won the second [[Derbi barceloní|derby]] of the season, with the only goal coming from Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/rcd-espanyol-fc-barcelona-thrilling-derby-win-0-1. |title=Thrilling derby win. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 March 2014 |access-date=30 March 2014}}</ref>

===April===
On 1 April, Barcelona drew in the first leg of the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the Champions League. The match against [[Atlético Madrid]] at the Camp Nou ended with a 1–1 draw. Neymar scored the goal for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-atletic-de-madrid-all-still-to-play-for-1-1 |title=All still to play for. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 April 2014 |access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref>
On 2 April, Barcelona was sanctioned by [[FIFA]] for international transfers of minors over various periods between 2009 and 2013. The sanction consisted in a transfer ban at both national and international level for two complete and consecutive transfer periods, together with a fine of [[Swiss franc|CHF]] 450,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2313003/index.html?intcmp=fifacom_hp_module_news |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140404204049/http://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2313003/index.html?intcmp=fifacom_hp_module_news |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 April 2014 |title=Spanish FA, FC Barcelona sanctioned for international transfers of minors. |publisher=FIFA |date=2 April 2014 |access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref> FIFA's regulations dictate that international transfers regarding minors are only accepted in three scenarios—the player's parents have moved to another country for non-related reasons; the move takes place within the European Union if the player is aged between 16 and 18, or the player's home is less than 50 kilometres from the national border being crossed.<ref>{{cite news |last=Corrigan |first=Dermot |url=http://www.espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1772107/fifa-hits-barcelona-transfer-ban |title=FIFA hits Barcelona with transfer ban |date=2 April 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Aarons |first=Ed |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/02/barcelona-transfer-ban-warning-signs-fifa |title=Barcelona fail to heed warning signs as Fifa cracks down on youth transfers |date=2 April 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> However, it was temporarily lifted until the appeal process, giving the club the chance to purchase players in the summer transfer window of 2014,<ref>{{cite news |last=Gibson |first=Owen |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/23/barcelona-transfer-ban-suspended-fifa |title=Barcelona's transfer ban suspended by Fifa pending appeal |date=23 April 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Ziegler |first=Martyn |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/barcelona-transfer-ban-fifa-suspend-twowindow-ban-pending-barcelonas-appeal-as-club-are-free-to-sign-players-in-summer-9277306.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/barcelona-transfer-ban-fifa-suspend-twowindow-ban-pending-barcelonas-appeal-as-club-are-free-to-sign-players-in-summer-9277306.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |title=Barcelona transfer ban: Barcelona free to sign players this summer after ban if lifted pending appeal |date=23 April 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |work=The Independent}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/301979.html |title=Barcelona transfer ban suspended |date=23 April 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

===May===
On 17 May, in a game where they needed to defeat [[Atlético Madrid]] (who eliminated them from the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|quarterfinals]] earlier in the year) to be crowned champions of La Liga for the 23rd time, they drew after Atlético defender [[Diego Godín]] headed in the equalizer in the 49th minute, giving Atlético the championship.<ref>{{cite news|last=Martin|first=Richard|title=Barcelona 1 Atletico Madrid 1, La Liga: match report|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/10838338/Barcelona-v-Atletico-Madrid-La-Liga-live.html|access-date=17 May 2014|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|location=London|date=17 May 2014}}</ref>

===From the youth system===
{{Fb fys header |age=y}}
